comments.body: This results in it basically ignoring the old `[main]` option since it will always either be the new `default_ssl_mode` if it exists or `None`. So will need a little extra logic if you want to still accept the old value (either a try/except without using `.get` or split it up so you get the new var, check if it's `None`, and then check the old var if so).
comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -171,7 +171,7 @@ def __init__(
         self.binary_display = c['main'].get('binary_display')
 
         # set ssl_mode if a valid option is provided in a config file, otherwise None
-        ssl_mode = c["main"].get("ssl_mode", None)
+        ssl_mode = c["connection"].get("default_ssl_mode", None) or c["main"].get("ssl_mode", None)
